setting.or: କୋଣାର୍କ ପାଖରେ ଆଜିର ଏକ କାଳ୍ପନିକ ବସତି। ଦିନୁଙ୍କ ଛୋଟ କାମଘରରେ ହାଲୁକା ନମୁନା ତିଆରି। ବାର ବର୍ଷର ତାରା ତାଙ୍କ ଭାଣିଜୀ; ଦିନୁ ତା’ ମାଆଙ୍କ ସାନଭାଇ, ବୟସ ଅଣଚାଳିଶ। ଦଶ ବର୍ଷର କାନୁ ପଡ଼ୋଶୀ ଓ ସାଙ୍ଗ। ଏହା ଧରମାର ଲୋକକଥା ବା ମନ୍ଦିର ନିର୍ମାଣର ଦୃଶ୍ୟ ନୁହେଁ।
setting.en: A fictional present-day settlement near Konark. Light model-making in Dinu’s small workshop. Twelve-year-old Tara is his niece; thirty-nine-year-old Dinu is her mother’s younger brother. Ten-year-old Kanu is a neighbour and friend. This is separate from the Dharama legend and the temple’s construction.

wardrobe.or: ତାରାର ସୋରିଷ ହଳଦିଆ ସାଧା କୁର୍ତ୍ତା, ମୋଡ଼ା ହାତ, ଗାଢ଼ ଧୂସର ସିଧା ପ୍ୟାଣ୍ଟ, ଚପଲ ଓ ଛୋଟ କେଶ। କେବଳ କାମ ଟେବୁଲ୍ ପାଖରେ କ୍ରିମ୍ କପଡ଼ା ଏପ୍ରନ୍, ପଛେ ଗଣ୍ଠି ଓ ଆଗେ ଗୋଟିଏ ପକେଟ୍। ଦିନୁଙ୍କ ମଳିନ ନୀଳ ସୂତା ସାର୍ଟର ହାତ ମୋଡ଼ା, ଢିଲା ଧୂସର ପ୍ୟାଣ୍ଟ, ଚପଲ ଓ ନିଜ ଡାହାଣ ଅଣ୍ଟାରେ କ୍ରିମ୍ ଗାମୁଛା; ନୂଆ ଦୃଶ୍ୟ ଅନୁସାରେ ତା’ ଧାରରେ ସରୁ ଲାଲ ରେଖା। କାନୁର ମାଟିଆ ଲାଲ ଛୋଟ ଚେକ୍ ସାର୍ଟ, ମଳିନ ନୀଳ ପ୍ୟାଣ୍ଟର ମୋଡ଼ା ତଳ ଓ ଚପଲ। ଏଗୁଡ଼ିକ ସମକାଳୀନ କାମର ପୋଷାକ; ଐତିହାସିକ କାରିଗରଙ୍କ ପ୍ରମାଣିତ ସଜ ନୁହେଁ।
wardrobe.en: Tara wears a plain mustard kurta with rolled sleeves, straight charcoal trousers, sandals and a practical bob. At the worktable only: a cream cloth apron tied at the back, with one front pocket. Dinu wears a faded-blue cotton work shirt with rolled sleeves, loose grey trousers and sandals; a cream gamucha at his anatomical right waist has narrow red end stripes as in the newer scene study. Kanu wears a small rust-check shirt, muted-blue trousers with rolled hems and sandals. These are contemporary work clothes, not authenticated historical artisan dress.

continuity.or: ଏକ ଛୋଟ ହାଲୁକା କାଗଜ ଟ୍ରେ, ଚାରି ତଳ ଭାଙ୍ଗ ଓ ଆଗରୁ କଟା ଟ୍ୟାବ୍। ତିନି କୋଣ ଆଗରୁ ବନ୍ଧା; ତାରା ଶେଷ କୋଣର ଟ୍ୟାବ୍ ଖୋସେ। କାନୁ ତଳ ଧରେ। କଇଁଚି ବା ଧାରୁଆ ଯନ୍ତ୍ର ନାହିଁ। ଶେଷରେ ଗୋଟିଏ ପେନ୍‌ସିଲ୍ ରଖାଯାଏ।
continuity.en: One small light paper tray with scored folds and tabs cut earlier. Three corners are secured; Tara tucks the final corner tab while Kanu holds the base. No scissors or sharp tools in this scene. One pencil goes into the finished tray.

performance.or: ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ପାଇଁ ଆଗୁଆ ହାତ → ପିଲାର କଥା ଶୁଣି ଥମିବା → ଅପେକ୍ଷାର ଅଭ୍ୟାସ → ନିଜ ତରତରକୁ ନେଇ ହସ।
performance.en: A hand reaching too soon → stopping to hear the child → practising waiting → laughing at his own hurry.

observations: Tara screenleft, Dinu centre/back, Kanu screenright. Maintain this staging through all four beats.
Natural-v2 is a separate stone-wheel scene: do not bring its stone wheel, ruler, bowl or scattered tools into the paper-tray film. This film uses only the light paper tray and one pencil.
Dinu wears a plain faded-blue shirt: graphite hatching in the pencil storyboard is not a textile check. The waist gamucha is on his anatomical RIGHT, with narrow red end stripes from natural-v2.
Kanu wears small rust checks; Tara has a practical bob, plain mustard kurta and cream work apron. Do not distribute Odisha motifs over the costumes.
Pencil storyboard shows the open front-left tray corner; three other corners are closed. The film must actually show the last tab entering and staying in its slot before hands release.
Dinu reaches toward the tray but stops BEFORE contact, then places both hands behind his back. Do not merge his hand with Tara’s.
One pencil stays on the table until Kanu picks it up after the tray holds. It must travel visibly from table to hand to tray; do not duplicate it.
Background shelves and table perspective should be stable, with no extra characters. The exact tray shape/scale should not change between views.

Model sheets confirm Tara apron back bow/one front pocket and short bob; Dinu curled hair/moustache and the hands-behind-back stance; Kanu short cropped hair, shirt chest pocket and rolled trouser hems. Preserve these identities.
The early Dinu model gamucha is plain cream; selected natural-v2 adds narrow red end stripes. Follow the newer selected scene consistently rather than alternating.

text.en: Wait a moment, Mamu. Can I try again?
I was the one in a hurry.
